title: Rosalind and the Ledger
premise: In the winter of the great storms, Sable Almeida keeps the lighthouse at Greywater Point and guards a family secret: their late husband's ledger, which records payments received for silencing witnesses to a shipping scandal. When a sealed letter arrives naming the Almeidas as accomplices, Sable must decide whether to burn the ledger or use it to bargain. As the river freezes and evacuation orders come, only one berth remains on the last ferry before the ice breaks—and Sable must choose between saving their daughter Rosalind, who knows nothing of the ledger, or her uncle Tobias, who helped write it. In the end, Sable gives the berth to Rosalind, surrenders the ledger to the magistrate, and stays behind at the light, choosing truth over blood and discovering that memory, honestly kept, is the only inheritance worth leaving.
about_author: Beatrix Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime correspondence from coastal lighthouse stations. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of other people's crimes.

chapters.title: The Weight of Glass
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Establishes daily life at Greywater Point: trimming wicks, logging weather, raising daughter Rosalind alone since the storms took her husband Edric's boat. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as routine, and the first hint that Edric left things unsaid.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Sable finds a waterlogged crate washed ashore containing papers bearing Edric's handwriting—pages torn from a ledger she has never seen. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: unease; the dead husband begins to feel like a stranger.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Oil Room
chapters.summary: Sable discovers the full ledger hidden beneath the oil store: dated entries recording payments 'for silence kept' tied to the Meridian Shipping wreck two winters past. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve—she hides it again rather than destroy it.

chapters.title: Rosalind Counts the Days
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, age fourteen, sharp-eyed and restless. She notices her mother's changed behavior and the ferry schedule posted early. Emotional beat: adolescent suspicion; she decides to find out what her mother is hiding.

chapters.title: A Letter Under Seal
chapters.summary: A magistrate's sealed letter arrives by coastal runner: the Almeida name appears among those implicated in the Meridian affair; an inquiry convenes when the ice breaks. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the trap closing—invisibility was always an illusion.

chapters.title: Tobias Comes Ashore
chapters.summary: Edric's brother Tobias arrives unannounced, charming and desperate, asking pointed questions about 'papers.' POV alternates Sable and Rosalind watching him. Emotional beat: loyalty strained—family arriving feels like surveillance.

chapters.title: Entries in Another Hand
chapters.summary: Sable studies the ledger closely and realizes some entries are in Tobias's handwriting, not Edric's. Flashback chapter to Edric's final visit home, uneasy and evasive. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing grief.

chapters.title: The Ferry Manifest
chapters.summary: Evacuation orders posted ahead of the worst storm season on record: one berth per household on the last ferry before the river freezes solid. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: hope curdling—she understands the berth is a choice, and choices have losers.

chapters.title: Silence Kept
chapters.summary: Tobias confesses partially: he and Edric took Meridian money to bury witness statements after the wreck; he claims Edric meant to confess. POV: Tobias via Sable's listening ear. Emotional beat: pity wrestling with anger.

chapters.title: What Rosalind Read
chapters.summary: Rosalind finds and reads the ledger, learning her father's complicity and her mother's concealment. Confrontation in the lamp room. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the shattering of the father she mourned; fury at being protected into ignorance.

chapters.title: The Storm That Named Itself
chapters.summary: The great storm hits early; the light must be kept burning through the night while the inquiry letter sits unanswered. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: duty as anchor—tending the flame while everything else burns.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Ice
chapters.summary: Tobias proposes destroying the ledger and taking the berth himself, promising silence; Sable counters that the ledger is now her only protection. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic of survival versus conscience.

chapters.title: Witness at Greywater
chapters.summary: A young magistrate's clerk, stranded by the storm, shelters at the station and recognizes the Almeida name. POV: clerk's brief third-person interlude filtered through Sable's hospitality. Emotional beat: paranoia—the house itself feels watched.

chapters.title: Mother, Daughter, Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable finally tells Rosalind everything, including why she hid it: fear that truth would cost them the berth, the name, each other. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: reconciliation not yet, but honesty as first repair.

chapters.title: The Berth Question
chapters.summary: The ferry master confirms: one seat. Tobias argues precedent (male heir), Rosalind argues innocence, Sable says nothing and cannot sleep. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: terror of being measured and found lighter than an uncle's guilt.

chapters.title: Edric's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Deciphering a smudged final page, Sable finds Edric recorded his intention to testify before he drowned—possibly not an accident. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief rekindled as purpose; the ledger becomes Edric's unfinished sentence.

chapters.title: Night of the Broken Lamp
chapters.summary: Sabotage: the lamp glass is shattered and the ledger goes missing during the night watch. Suspicion falls on everyone. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: violation and vertigo—the keeper who failed the light.

chapters.title: Tobias at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Sable catches Tobias boarding the supply skiff with the ledger hidden in his coat; confrontation on the ice-slick rocks. He admits Edric's drowning may not have been chance. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the climax of betrayal—loyalty dies so truth can live.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Climax. At the dock, Sable puts Rosalind in the berth, hands the recovered ledger to the waiting magistrate's clerk, and lets the ferry pull away with her daughter and without her. POV: alternating Sable and Rosalind across widening water. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship—choosing which inheritance survives.

chapters.title: Testimony by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Sable gives her account to the inquiry at the station itself, the lighthouse beam sweeping the room like a slow searchlight. Tobias is taken; the Meridian men are named. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: exhaustion and strange lightness—truth spoken aloud weighs nothing.

chapters.title: Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Spring. The river cracks open; the first boat carries a letter from Rosalind and news of the trial's outcome. Sable reads it in the lamp room. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: forgiveness beginning its long crossing toward her.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Hand
chapters.summary: Resolution. Rosalind returns at summer's end; together they begin a new ledger—honest entries, kept openly, the first line reading 'what we carried.' POV: shared. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed; memory kept in daylight.
